input_visibility_diagnostic.note: Plan 09-06b corrected the objective: train_ndt1 and every scoring path now hide the scored positions from the encoder, so hidden_* is the published number and reproduces co_bps.per_session / co_bps.pooled on the same seeded mask. visible_* leaks the scored counts back into the encoder, which is what the superseded objective did on every forward pass. visible_* is an out-of-distribution probe for a model trained on hidden inputs; it is not a corrected, better or alternative result and must not be quoted as one.

co_bps.margin_rationale: Observed pooled held-out co-bps on real primate M1 spikes is 0.4096 bits/spike against the train-split mean-rate null. The margin 0.054 is 13.1% of it: the fraction Phase 4 used when it set 0.05 against an observed 0.3804, applied unchanged so that the observation is the only input to this derivation. Phase 4's 0.05 was calibrated on a purpose-built learnable synthetic sinusoid and does not transfer to real spikes. What the gate asserts is exactly 'better than the constant per-channel mean-rate null by more than 0.054 bits/spike' and nothing more; whether that is a meaningful demonstration of non-trivial reconstruction depends on the size of the observation it was derived from, which is recorded beside it at co_bps.pooled.train_null.
co_bps.trajectory_note: Held-out pooled co-bps measured at epoch 1, every 10 epochs, and at the 200-epoch cap, against the same two nulls as the headline and on the same seeded mask. The reported value is the row at the cap. No epoch was selected from this curve, and the checkpoint saved is the model at the cap, not the model at whichever epoch scored best.

convergence.rule: NO stopping rule. Train to the 200-epoch cap, record held-out co-bps along the way, publish the whole trajectory, and report the value AT the cap. No epoch is selected after the fact, so there is no stopping decision to audit

loso_summary.budget_note: The rotation ran at 60 epochs per fold against the pooled run's 200. That is a COST decision pre-registered before the run, not a result decision: the four folds are 21,396 training windows to the pooled 7,132, so a full-cap rotation would have cost roughly 11.5 h of CPU on top of the headline run. 60 is the epoch cap Plan 09-06c had already committed, so it is an inherited constant rather than a number chosen for this run. Every fold got the same budget and ran to it. The consequence is that the folds are LESS trained than the pooled model, so a cross-session number here is a floor for that budget and must not be compared against the pooled figure as though both were trained equally.

superseded_rule_stopped_at_floor.note: Plan 09-06c. Corrected input-masking objective, gradient clipping at max_norm 1.0, and a stopping rule pre-registered on the training loss. Pooled held-out co-bps 0.0713 against the train-split mean-rate null and 0.0432 against the pooled test-mean null, at 12 epochs. The objective was correct and the numerics were guarded; what supersedes it is the BUDGET and the FORWARD-PASS OVERFLOW. The stopping rule fired at its own 12-epoch floor (convergence.fired_at_floor = true) and a pre-registered probe then measured that epochs 12 to 60 move the loss only 1.3% while pooled co-bps rises 4.2x, so this run stopped far short of the curve; and masked_poisson_nll could still overflow float32 exp, which cost one LOSO fold of four. These numbers must not be quoted as this repository's held-out co-bps on real primate M1 spikes. They may be quoted only as what a 12-epoch clipped run under a loss-plateau stopping rule gave, with the qualifier that the rule stopped at its floor.

superseded_truncated_budget.note: Every number in this block was measured under the CORRECTED input-masking objective (Plan 09-06b hid the scored positions from the encoder, and tests/test_masked_input_isolation.py holds that in place), so unlike superseded_visible_input_objective it is not measuring self-reconstruction. What supersedes it is the budget and the numerics, not the objective. It was produced at a fixed 12-epoch budget inherited from Phase 4, where that budget had been calibrated against the DEFECTIVE objective and reached a 43 percent loss reduction; under the corrected objective it reached 6 percent and the loss was still descending monotonically at about 0.0007 per epoch when the budget ran out, so the pooled 0.006214627530704778 is a floor at that budget and not an asymptote. The run also had no gradient clipping: one of the four LOSO folds diverged and the committed slow gate diverged outright. Plan 09-06c added torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ at max_norm 1.0 and replaced the fixed budget with a stopping rule pre-registered on the TRAINING LOSS before the run, then re-derived every dependent number. These values MAY be quoted as what a 12-epoch unclipped run under the corrected objective produced, and MUST NOT be quoted as this repository's converged co-bps.

input_visibility_diagnostic.note: train_ndt1 feeds the encoder the UNMASKED counts and uses the mask only to select which positions the Poisson NLL is summed over, so a scored position is visible to the model that predicts it. visible_* reproduces the committed numbers on the same seeded mask; hidden_* re-scores the same checkpoint with the scored positions zeroed in the encoder input. The checkpoint was never trained with hidden inputs, so hidden_* is a floor and visible_* is a ceiling, not a corrected value.

co_bps.margin_rationale: Observed pooled held-out co-bps on real primate M1 spikes is 1.9116 bits/spike against the train-split mean-rate null. The margin 0.25 is 13.1% of it, the same fraction Phase 4 used when it set 0.05 against an observed 0.3804 -- high enough above the 0.0 null to mean something, low enough below the observation that run-to-run variation cannot flake the gate. Phase 4's 0.05 was calibrated on a purpose-built learnable synthetic sinusoid and does not transfer to real spikes.

NDT1ANE.forward performs no input masking either.
superseded_visible_input_objective.note: Every number in this block was measured under the objective Plan 09-06 shipped, in which ndt1.train.train_ndt1 called model(targets) on the UNMASKED spike counts and used the mask only to select which positions the Poisson NLL was summed over. The encoder could read the observed count at every position it was scored on, so these values measure self-reconstruction plus context, not context alone. They are retained because 09-06-SUMMARY.md and 09-training-evidence.md quote them and a reader must be able to look them up, and because deleting a number a repository has published is not a correction. THEY MUST NOT BE QUOTED as a decoder result. Plan 09-06b corrected the objective (ndt1.train.masked_forward + ndt1.loss.hide_scored_positions, guarded by tests/test_masked_input_isolation.py) and re-measured everything; the co_bps, losses, loso and checkpoint keys at the top level of this file are the current numbers.
